name: Variable-slip wind turbine generator (Type 2)
summary: A wind turbine using a wound-rotor induction generator with controlled external rotor resistance to widen the slip range.
description: A Type 2 wind turbine uses a wound-rotor induction generator whose rotor circuit is connected to a variable resistance, usually switched by power electronics mounted on the rotor. Raising the rotor resistance lets the slip increase to around ten per cent, which softens torque peaks from gusts while the stator stays connected directly to the network.

Drawings show the generator circle with rotor slip-ring or rotor-winding marks and a resistor element with a variable arrow attached to the rotor side. The stator side follows the same path as a Type 1 machine: soft starter, capacitor compensation and step-up transformer.

Energy dissipated in the rotor resistance is lost as heat, so the symbol says nothing about efficiency or about any capability to deliver reactive power. Fault ride-through behaviour and resistor ratings must be read from the turbine model data.
readingNotes: The variable resistor on the rotor side is a slip control element, not a braking resistor or a load.
Stator-side compensation capacitors are still normally present.
drawingChecklist: Reference turbine model data for dynamic studies.
distinction: A Type 2 turbine dissipates rotor energy in resistance; a doubly-fed generator returns rotor power to the network through a converter.
